title: Jerk Chicken
subtitle: Jamaican spiced grilled chicken with scotch bonnet and allspice
excerpt: Chicken pieces marinated in a fiery paste of scotch bonnet, allspice, thyme, and spring onion, then grilled over high heat until charred and fragrant. The national street food of Jamaica.

recipe.sourceNotes: Jerk is a style of cooking originating with the Maroons of Jamaica, communities of escaped enslaved Africans who developed the technique of smoking meat over pimento wood in the Blue Mountains. The key spices are allspice (pimento) and scotch bonnet chilli, both native to the Caribbean. The word jerk refers both to the spice rub and the cooking technique. Jerk chicken is sold roadside throughout Jamaica cooked over oil-drum barbecues. The authentic preparation calls for pimento wood; hardwood charcoal is the best practical substitute for home cooking, giving a similar smoky char. Oven-grilling works but misses the smoke.

recipeTools.notes: Or cook over charcoal for authenticity.

content.text: Marinate the chicken overnight if you can: at minimum 4 hours, ideally 24 hours. The longer it sits in the jerk paste, the deeper the flavour penetrates. Score the chicken pieces through to the bone before marinating so the paste can reach the meat. The scotch bonnet is very hot: use gloves when handling it, or reduce the quantity if you want less heat. Do not remove all the seeds if you want the authentic fire.

Blend all the marinade ingredients together (scotch bonnet through to lime juice) until a coarse paste forms. Score the chicken pieces down to the bone. Coat thoroughly in the jerk paste. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.

If using a barbecue, cook over medium-hot coals for 30 to 40 minutes, turning every 10 minutes, until the chicken is charred on the outside and cooked through to the bone. If using a griddle pan or grill, cook on medium-high heat for 15 minutes per side until cooked through, charred, and sticky.
Rest for 5 minutes. Serve with rice and peas, fried plantain, and a squeeze of lime.
